summary.lead: Ship Insights small, price it with evidence.

projects.name: Insights
projects.aka: Heard as "In Sites" in the captions
projects.what: A new feature that tells a support manager why tickets went up and what to do about it, on one screen. It goes to ten beta customers first.
projects.status: Scope locked to five steps. Beta opens 23 Nov if the connector is ready on 20 Nov.

blocks.label: Customer journey
blocks.title: What Insights does for a support manager

items.title: Connect
items.sub: The manager: links Zendesk and Jira in two minutes, no engineer.

cols.label: Insights does
cols.text: Pulls in ticket history and release notes.

cols.label: She gets
cols.text: A setup she can finish alone.

items.title: Spot
items.sub: The manager: sees tickets about login up 40% since Thursday.

cols.label: Insights does
cols.text: Finds spikes by topic, not just totals.

cols.label: She gets
cols.text: The spike, the topic and the date it started.

cols.label: Why it matters
cols.text: No more guessing in a spreadsheet.

items.title: Explain
items.sub: The manager: learns the spike came from one release.

cols.label: Insights does
cols.text: Links the spike to the release note and the first ten customers who hit it.

cols.label: Why it matters
cols.text: The hard part, and the reason to buy.

cols.label: Insights does
cols.text: Offers a help article, a reply macro, or a bug ticket with the evidence attached.

cols.label: She gets
cols.text: A next step in one click.

items.title: Report
items.sub: The head of support: reads one page every Friday.

cols.label: Insights does
cols.text: Sends what went up, why, and what the team did.

cols.label: She gets
cols.text: Her Monday report, done for her.

cols.label: Why it matters
cols.text: Leaders see the value every week.

blocks.label: Inputs
blocks.title: What customers plug in
blocks.intro: Explain only works if Insights has these three things. Release notes are the risky one, so they get a simple upload screen.

items.title: Ticket history
items.text: From Zendesk, connected in two minutes

items.title: Release notes
items.text: Half live in Google Docs: paste a link or drop a file

items.title: Customer list
items.text: With plan sizes, to rank who is hurt most

quote.text: So we give them a simple upload screen. Paste a link or drop a file. I'll design it this week.

items.title: SOC 2 report
items.text: The June report goes with every beta invite.

items.title: Data note
items.text: One page on how we handle their data, by Friday.

items.title: Custom dashboards
items.text: Would add a month. Out of scope.

projects.name: Pricing test
projects.what: Sales and Finance disagree on how to charge for Insights. Instead of arguing, both options are tested on beta trials for two weeks.
projects.status: Two-week test starts with the beta. Price chosen in week 3.

blocks.label: Conflict resolution diagram
blocks.title: Starter tier or usage add-on?
blocks.goal: More paying teams without hurting margin

sides.position: Add a starter tier at $29 a month for teams under 10 agents.
sides.because: Small teams can't pay today's price, and usage pricing makes their bill unpredictable.

sides.position: Sell Insights as an add-on, priced per 1,000 tickets.
sides.because: A cheap tier pulls big customers down. Last year's discount plan slowed MRR growth for two quarters.

blocks.way: test both on beta trials for two weeks, then decide with the numbers.

items.label: A price wins if
list: Revenue per account does not drop

projects.name: Launch plan
projects.what: Three weeks from beta to public launch, with a gate that must pass before each next step.
projects.status: Agreed. Week 1 starts with the beta on 23 Nov.

items.label: Week 1
items.title: Beta with 10 customers
items.text: Ten customers use Insights on their real tickets.
items.gate: Gate: no critical bugs, connector errors under 1%.

items.label: Week 2
items.title: Public launch
items.text: Campaign goes live with the agency.
items.gate: Gate: 6 of 10 beta customers use it every week.

items.label: Week 3
items.title: Review and price
items.text: Read the price test and the usage numbers.
items.gate: Pick the price with the evidence.

items.label: Track
items.title: Time saved per manager
items.text: Needs a baseline: ask beta customers first.

decisions.text: The beta opens on 23 Nov, if the connector is green on 20 Nov.
decisions.why: The Zendesk connector is the only thing blocking the beta.

decisions.text: Version 1 is five steps. No custom dashboards.
decisions.why: Custom dashboards would add a month.

decisions.text: Test both prices on beta trials for two weeks.
decisions.why: Sales and Finance want the same outcome, and nobody knows which price gets there.

decisions.text: A price wins if it beats 14% trial conversion without lowering revenue per account.
decisions.why: Agreed before the test, so the result can't be argued later.

decisions.text: Launch in three weeks, with a gate before each step.
decisions.why: Each step only starts when the previous one proves itself.

decisions.text: Track weekly active teams, tickets explained, conversion and time saved.
decisions.why: These show whether Insights is used and worth paying for.

open.q: Do existing customers get Insights free for three months?
open.why: Sarah leans no, but the renewal side wasn't in the room.
open.close: Nadia's view from renewal calls, plus the cost.

open.q: Who answers AI questions on sales calls?
open.why: There's no sales engineer yet, and Marco can't join every call.
open.close: Name an owner, or plan a hire.

open.q: Are customers' release notes clean enough to explain spikes?
open.why: About half keep them in Google Docs.
open.close: Try it on the beta customers' real notes.
open.next: Check during week 1 of the beta.

open.q: How much time does Insights actually save?
open.why: Nobody has measured the Monday report today.
open.close: A baseline from each beta customer.
